capabilities: Sync a vault through a self-hosted server from desktop, mobile, and the command line
Merge non-overlapping edits and keep conflict copies instead of overwriting
Restore deleted files from the server trash and browse per-file revision history
Encrypt vault contents and file names end-to-end with password and recovery phrase
Choose which Obsidian settings (appearance, hotkeys, plugins) sync between devices
extras: The README addresses Obsidian's review flags directly: it explains the desktop direct file system access (Node fs with atomic writes and fsync), states there is no telemetry, and discloses that a Rust-compiled WebAssembly sync core is embedded in main.js with build provenance attestations. A hosted variant (Selfsync Cloud) exists but is a separate plugin; this plugin has no accounts or subscriptions. Also covers read-only devices, light-device download limits, and a CLI that syncs plain folders without Obsidian.
problem: Obsidian's built-in sync is a paid hosted service, and generic file-sync tools can silently lose overlapping edits or deletions.
summary: Self-hosted vault sync through your own server with diff3 auto-merge, conflict copies, deleted-file trash, revision history and optional end-to-end encryption.
